title: L4-L5 intact ROM at ±7.5 Nm, polysegmental specimens (Wilke 2025)

quantity.name: ROM
quantity.definition: full-range value (both directions summed), mean ± SD

source.authors: Wilke HJ, Kienle A, Werner K, Liebsch C
source.sample: Ulm institutional database 1995-2024: intact human lumbar FSUs T12-S1 from mono- (n~300) and polysegmental specimens (n~290), 36 lumbar publications (Table 4); FE n=590, LB n=596, AR n=590

protocol.summary: Pure moments 7.5 Nm (lumbar) without axial preload; five uncontrolled DOF unconstrained (gimbal on travelling gantry with balancing weights); caudal end rigidly fixed, cranial end to gimbal; PMMA half-embedding; quasi-static 0.5-1 deg/s; 3.5 cycles, 3rd full cycle evaluated; ROM and NZ from the hysteresis curve (zero points by polynomial fit); rotations by RVDT, goniometric linkage, Zebris ultrasound or Vicon (<=0.1 deg). Outliers beyond 2 SD excluded.
how_to_simulate: Fix the caudal vertebra of the FSU; cranial vertebra free in all DOF; no preload
Apply ±7.5 Nm pure moments in flexion/extension, left/right lateral bending, left/right axial rotation (3 cycles; evaluate 3rd)
Report full-range ROM (sum of both directions) and NZ at 0 Nm per plane
Compare with median ± MAD of the level
protocol.notes: ROM and NZ are both-direction totals. Per-level data mix monosegmental and polysegmental specimens (polysegmental ROM at L4-L5 is 10-27% lower, Fig 6). Thoracic (5 Nm, ± rib cage) and cervical (2.5 Nm) data exist in the paper but belong to other groups.

extraction.uncertainty: means ±0.05 deg, SD ±0.15 deg (upper whisker); AR NZ means read at half-saturation edge (0.68 vs 0.63; the paper reports -8%)
extraction.check_notes: Ratios reproduce printed differences: FE ROM -10.5% (printed -10%), LB -11%, AR -27%, FE NZ +17% (+18%), LB NZ +24% (+23%), AR NZ -7% (-8%).
